body: The Airbus A350-900ULR has operated the world's two longest flights — Singapore Airlines' Singapore–Newark and Singapore–JFK services — since deliveries began in 2018, and the A350-1000ULR will start reaching Qantas in 2027 for nonstop Sydney–New York and Sydney–London services. The Boeing 787-9, the closest competitor on range and ultra-long-haul economics, flies four of the world's ten longest nonstop services yet has never had a ULR or extended-range version. The first reason is not technical but commercial: no customer has asked for one. The A350-900ULR was built specifically so Singapore Airlines could fly Singapore–New York nonstop reliably, and the A350-1000ULR answers a Qantas request for Sydney–London with a reasonable payload; both are niche aircraft built for one customer's extreme requirement, and Qantas reportedly holds exclusivity rights preventing other airlines from taking A350-1000ULRs until all 12 of its aircraft have arrived. If an airline wanted a ULR 787-9 and was willing to pay for it, Boeing would certainly build it — but for almost all airlines the standard 787-9 already has more than enough range.

Even with demand, the 787-9 has less room to grow than the A350. At the edge of its range the A350 is largely limited by fuel capacity, and the ULR variants' main advantage is significantly greater fuel capacity. The 787-9 is instead limited by its Maximum Takeoff Weight, which restricts how much fuel and payload it can carry; on its longest scheduled flight, Perth–London, Qantas regularly has to block seats because the aircraft reaches MTOW before every seat can be filled. Boeing recently raised the 787-9's MTOW from 254.7 tons to 259.2 tons, adding about 310 NM (570 km) of range, but the structure and landing gear are approaching their weight limits, and any further increase would likely require significant structural strengthening and a landing-gear redesign — an expensive project that may not be necessary today.

The comparison table shows the positioning gap: the A350-900 has an MTOW of 283 tons, a range of 8,500 NM (15,750 km) with typical payload, 270 to 300 seats and 1,140 orders; the A350-1000, 322 tons, 9,000 NM (16,700 km), 300 to 330 seats and 373 orders; the 787-9, 259.2 tons, 7,875 NM (14,585 km), 250 to 280 seats and 1,493 orders; the 787-10, 260.4 tons, 6,760 NM (12,519 km), 290 to 320 seats and 587 orders. The 787-9's appeal is cost: it burns less fuel than the A350-900 in almost all circumstances, and its smaller size and lower operating cost open routes that were not previously economical, doing about 95% of what the A350-900 does for less money — which is why it has become the most successful widebody aircraft variant of all time. The 787-10 is a simple stretch of the 787-9 with largely the same MTOW and fuel capacity, trading range for payload, while the 787-8 has a lower MTOW of 227.9 tons and a shorter range than the 787-9, with sales dried up as airlines prefer the more economical 787-9 and 787-10. The A350 remains the final answer for the world's longest flights: the A350-900ULR reached its capability by raising MTOW to 280 tons, blocking the forward cargo hold and unlocking more of the existing tank volume through software changes, while the A350-1000ULR adds an integrated rear centre tank holding over 20,000 liters (5,280 gallons) for more than 1,000 NM (1,850 km) of extra range.
en.summary: Boeing has never built a ULR 787-9 mainly because no customer asked for one; both Airbus A350 ULR variants were built for a single customer's extreme requirement. Even with demand, the 787-9 is limited by maximum takeoff weight rather than fuel capacity, and it does about 95% of what the A350-900 does at lower cost.
en.title: Why Boeing has never built an ultra-long-range 787 — and what stops it

body: 空中巴士A350-900ULR自2018年交付以來，執飛全球最長的兩條航線——新加坡航空新加坡—紐華克與新加坡—甘迺迪航線；A350-1000ULR則將自2027年起交付澳航，投入雪梨—紐約與雪梨—倫敦不中停航線。與之相比，波音787-9雖然執飛全球10條最長不中停航線中的4條，卻從未推出ULR或增程版本。原因首先不在技術，而在市場：沒有客戶要求過這樣的飛機。A350-900ULR是為新加坡航空的新加坡—紐約不中停航線量身打造，A350-1000ULR則回應澳航雪梨—倫敦合理載量不中停的需求；兩者皆是為單一客戶極端需求設計的小眾機型，據報導，澳航持有排他權利，其他航空公司須待澳航12架全數交付後才能接收A350-1000ULR。若有航空公司願意出資訂購ULR版787-9，波音勢必會開發；但對絕大多數航空公司而言，標準版787-9的航程已綽綽有餘。

即便有需求，787-9的改裝空間也比A350小。A350在航程極限主要受油箱容量限制，ULR版本正是大幅增加可用油量；787-9則受最大起飛重量限制，限制了可攜帶的燃油與酬載。澳航伯斯—倫敦航線是787-9最長定期航班，飛機常在座位全滿前就達到最大起飛重量，航空公司因而須經常鎖住部分座位。波音近期已將787-9最大起飛重量由254.7噸提高至259.2噸，航程增加約310海里（570公里）；但機體結構與起落架的承重能力已近上限，再提高重量可能需要大幅結構強化與起落架重新設計，成本高昂且現階段未必必要。

數據對比顯示兩者的定位差異：A350-900最大起飛重量283噸、典型酬載航程8,500海里（15,750公里）、270至300座、訂單1,140架；A350-1000為322噸、9,000海里（16,700公里）、300至330座、訂單373架；787-9為259.2噸、7,875海里（14,585公里）、250至280座、訂單1,493架；787-10為260.4噸、6,760海里（12,519公里）、290至320座、訂單587架。787-9的優勢在於營運成本低：幾乎在所有情況下燃油消耗都低於A350-900，機身較小、購置與營運成本較低，能開闢以往不具經濟效益的航線。787-10則是787-9的加長型，最大起飛重量與油箱容量大致相同，載客更多、航程更短；787-8的最大起飛重量僅227.9噸，航程反而短於787-9，且銷售已枯竭。綜合來看，787-9已能滿足A350-900約95%的能力，卻更便宜——這正是它成為史上最成功廣體客機衍生型的原因；而A350仍是全球最長航線的最終答案：A350-900ULR將最大起飛重量提高至280噸、封閉前方貨艙並透過軟體釋放既有油箱容積，A350-1000ULR則新增整合式後中央油箱，油量增加逾20,000公升（5,280加侖），航程增加逾1,000海里（1,850公里）。
zh.summary: 波音從未推出超長程版787-9，首要原因是沒有客戶要求；空中巴士A350-900ULR與A350-1000ULR皆為單一客戶的極端需求而生。即使有需求，787-9也受最大起飛重量限制，而非油箱容量；數據對比顯示787-9能做到A350-900約95%的能力，成本卻更低。
zh.title: 波音為何造不出超長程版787飛機：市場需求、起飛重量與油箱容量的三重限制
